proposed_branch: Use the same 10-atom CaBe2Ge2 framework, cell, Pt/Ge ordering, and refined coordinates in P4/nmm, with each paired rare-earth site occupied by La0.5Ce0.5 instead of fully ordered La and Ce sites.
reason: The primary CIF is valid: it parses as a 10-atom primitive cell with La1Ce1Ge4Pt4, full occupancies, a=b=4.39880 A and c=10.03535 A, and inferred P4mm symmetry; its 2.480 A minimum contact and complete Pt-Ge coordination give no chemical veto. The tetragonal indexing covers the selected reflections, independent peak-height and integrated-intensity refinements converge near the submitted coordinates, and the other distinct Pt/Ge orbit-allocation families fit far worse. However, the decisive La/Ce ordering and symmetry choice is unsupported: every coordinate/intensity refinement in the trace used 50:50 La/Ce average scattering on the paired rare-earth sites, which instantiates the concrete P4/nmm disordered model, whereas the submitted CIF assumes full La/Ce order and lowers the symmetry to P4mm. A blind recalculation gives essentially identical integrated-intensity objectives (0.007512 ordered versus 0.007517 disordered, with at most a 0.17% line-intensity difference), so the data do not reject the absent P4/nmm occupancy realization. Another attempt is likely to add this materially different viable candidate.
